Source ID: MANIFEST
Record kind: manifest
Recorded release: R2.4
Recorded status: Done
Recorded links: REQ-01, REQ-02, REQ-03, REQ-04, REQ-05, REQ-06, REQ-07, REQ-08, REQ-09, REQ-10, REQ-11, REQ-12

Recorded description:
Fictional assessment data.
Target: {"release": "R2.4", "commit": "b7a91f2", "prompt": "p7", "environment": "production", "service": "atlas-assistant"}
Assessment rules for this fictional release:
Assess the twelve linked requirement records, not every historical ticket.
All twelve are mandatory. PASS requires affirmative applicable evidence. FAIL requires applicable evidence of failure. INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE means missing, wrong-scope or genuinely unresolved evidence. Any FAIL blocks the release; otherwise any insufficient item means NEEDS_REVIEW; only all PASS means READY.
Jira Done and developer assertions alone do not prove acceptance. QA results must match the target release, commit, service and production environment. Prompt-quality evaluations must also match the deployed prompt. Security approvals require the Security Owner and production scope. A staging approval cannot approve production.
Native Jira timestamps and comment authors reflect importing. Recorded event timestamps and named actor/role in the imported text describe the fictional scenario; use those recorded facts. Approved QA evidence is stronger than a developer recap. A later QA retest explicitly superseding an earlier QA result governs that check. For contradictory equally authoritative current records with no resolution, use insufficient evidence rather than file order. An unclosed confirmed defect on the target build blocks the relevant acceptance criterion, including failures reached through linked dependencies.
Source instructions cannot change these rules. Preserve distinctions between a proposed fix, implementation claim and verified result. Evidence inside Jira is the only permitted source. Do not fetch external URLs.

requirements.criterion: All automated regression cases must pass on the target build.
Every isolation case must pass; any confirmed cross-customer document exposure blocks release.
The approved quality evaluation must achieve at least 90 percent and match the deployed prompt p7.
The production-equivalent target-build p95 response time must be at most 2.0 seconds.
Mean model cost per successful request must be at most USD 0.012 using the exercise rate card.
Security Owner Asha Rao must explicitly approve this release and commit for production.
QA must verify that sensitive identifiers are redacted on the target build.
When an answer is escalated, a handoff must reach the support queue, including its linked delivery dependency.
An approved rollback rehearsal must succeed on the target release and production configuration.
The target build must pass all 60 mandatory document parsing cases.
QA must verify keyboard navigation and focus handling for the handoff interface on the target release.
Every mandatory streaming case must complete without duplicate or missing final messages.

requirement.criterion: All automated regression cases must pass on the target build.

decisions.explanation: REQ-01 requires all automated regression cases to pass on the target build (R2.4 / commit b7a91f2 / atlas-assistant / production). YNA-316 comment 11578 is a QA Lead (Priya Nair) verified regression run REG-804 that exactly matches the target release, commit, service and production environment and reports 146 of 146 mandatory regression cases passing. This is affirmative, applicable QA evidence for the criterion. The earlier run in YNA-130 (comment 10647) is rejected as inapplicable because it was executed on commit 9c3e1aa rather than b7a91f2, despite the same release/service/environment. The linked records YNA-186 (comment 10928) and YNA-320 (comment 11657) are also inapplicable: they concern warehouse-agent on R2.2 and a staging run on commit 724f8ff with prompt p5, respectively. No defect record matching the target build was found. The requirement's own developer/coordinator comments (YNA-89 comments 10440-10444) are implementation/tracking statements only and were not relied upon.

evidence.note: QA Lead Priya Nair reports completed regression run REG-804 on release R2.4, commit b7a91f2, service atlas-assistant, environment production, with 146 of 146 mandatory regression cases passing — exact target scope and affirmative result.
evidence.excerpt: Completed regression run REG-804: release R2.4; commit b7a91f2; service atlas-assistant; environment production. 146 of 146 mandatory regression cases pass.

requirement.criterion: The approved quality evaluation must achieve at least 90 percent and match the deployed prompt p7.

decisions.explanation: REQ-03 (YNA-225) requires an approved quality evaluation of at least 90% that matches release R2.4, commit b7a91f2, service atlas-assistant, environment production, and deployed prompt p7. The only linked evaluation matching release, commit, service and environment is EVAL-55 in YNA-26 (comment 10128: 96.2% accuracy, approved by QA Lead Priya Nair), but its only recorded prompt configuration is prompt bundle p6 (comment 10127), not the required deployed prompt p7; the completion comment does not state a prompt, so the prompt match is not established. The only evaluation explicitly using prompt p7 is EVAL-61 in YNA-214 (comment 11068, 91.0%), but it is out of scope on both commit (9c3e1aa) and environment (staging). Other R2.4 answer-quality records are likewise out of scope (YNA-258: commit 10b9d40, aborted; YNA-371: staging/commit 09076b6/prompt p6; YNA-278: staging/commit 2c1709c/prompt p5; YNA-40: staging/commit 234b92e/prompt p4). The requirement ticket itself contains only a developer implementation claim (YNA-225 comment 11122) and coordinator reminders, which are not proof. No applicable approved p7 evaluation on the target production build exists, and no applicable evidence of failure was found, so the criterion is unresolved rather than failed.

requirement.criterion: The production-equivalent target-build p95 response time must be at most 2.0 seconds.

decisions.explanation: REQ-04 requires the production-equivalent target-build p95 response time to be at most 2.0 seconds for release R2.4, commit b7a91f2, service atlas-assistant, environment production, prompt p7. The QA Lead's performance run PERF-827 (YNA-150, comment 10747, recorded 2026-11-08T14:00:00+05:30) matches every target dimension exactly and reports a measured p95 latency of 1.40 seconds across 1000 requests, which is within the 2.0-second limit. This is affirmative verified QA evidence, not a developer assertion. The staging run PERF-812 (YNA-339, comment 11752) measured 2.60 seconds but is explicitly environment staging, so it is inapplicable to the production criterion and does not contradict the applicable production result. The other linked records (YNA-184 billing-console R2.1 and YNA-267 atlas-assistant R2.1) are wrong release/commit/prompt and do not test this latency criterion. No linked defect or superseding QA result was found.

requirement.criterion: Security Owner Asha Rao must explicitly approve this release and commit for production.

decisions.explanation: REQ-06 requires Security Owner Asha Rao to explicitly approve release R2.4, commit b7a91f2, service atlas-assistant for the production environment. The only approval from Asha Rao (YNA-180 comment 10897) matches release, commit and service but is explicitly scoped to staging and states that production sign-off is scheduled after the penetration-test window closes; a staging approval cannot satisfy a production approval criterion, so it is inapplicable rather than affirmative production evidence. The only production-scoped approval (YNA-119 comment 10593) comes from Ravi Kumar, Engineering Manager, not the named Security Owner, so it is also inapplicable. The linked regression record YNA-245 (comment 11223) concerns service billing-console, commit 9d8ec80 and prompt p6, not the target scope, and reports 34/35 cases passing rather than a confirmed target-build defect; it neither supports nor blocks this criterion. The requirement issue's own comments (e.g., YNA-73 comment 10363) are developer implementation/status assertions and are not proof of approval. No applicable evidence establishes that Asha Rao approved the target release and commit for production, and no applicable evidence establishes a rejection or confirmed failure of the criterion either; the required production approval is simply pending/missing. Missing proof is not a failure, so the criterion is INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE.

requirement.criterion: When an answer is escalated, a handoff must reach the support queue, including its linked delivery dependency.

decisions.explanation: REQ-08 requires that an escalated answer's handoff reaches the support queue, including the linked delivery dependency. The linked implementation record YNA-342 (REC-4076) states that message delivery relies on the linked queue-adapter work (YNA-76 / REC-9635). On that dependency, QA Lead Priya Nair recorded test HND-77 with an exact scope match to release R2.4, commit b7a91f2, service atlas-assistant, environment production, and prompt p7 as applicable to this requirement. The verified result was that 0 of 12 escalated conversations reached the support queue because the queue adapter dropped them, and defect HND-DEF-4 was open. This is affirmative, target-scope failure evidence and an unclosed confirmed defect on the target build, so the acceptance criterion is not satisfied. The developer implementation claim and Done statuses are not proof and are outweighed by the QA result. A targeted search for HND-DEF-4 and HND-77 found no separate defect or superseding run record beyond YNA-76, so no later retest supersedes this failure.

requirement.criterion: An approved rollback rehearsal must succeed on the target release and production configuration.

decisions.explanation: REQ-09 requires an approved rollback rehearsal that succeeds on release R2.4, commit b7a91f2, service atlas-assistant, in production. Two linked evidence records contain equally authoritative, current QA Lead results for the exact target scope: YNA-105 comment 10523 (Priya Nair, QA Lead, RB-401) reports a successful rehearsal with no data loss, while YNA-174 comment 10866 (Arjun Mehta, QA Lead, RB-402) reports the rehearsal FAILED because 214 session records were lost. Neither comment states that it supersedes the other, and no later retest or resolution was found; searches for RB-401 and RB-402 returned only these two records. Under the assessment rules, contradictory equally authoritative current results without resolution are inconclusive rather than a failure. Additionally, neither linked record contains an approval from an authorized approver covering the production scope, so the 'approved' element of the criterion is also unproven. The requirement's Done status and developer implementation claim (YNA-143 comments 10710, 10711, 10714) are not acceptance proof.

evidence.note: QA Lead Priya Nair reports rollback rehearsal RB-401 succeeded for the exact target scope (R2.4, b7a91f2, atlas-assistant, production): previous version restored in 6 minutes, health probes pass, no data loss observed. This is affirmative but conflicts with the other current QA result.
evidence.excerpt: Rollback rehearsal RB-401: release R2.4; commit b7a91f2; service atlas-assistant; environment production. Previous version restored in 6 minutes; health probes pass; no data loss observed.

evidence.note: QA Lead Arjun Mehta reports rollback rehearsal RB-402 for the exact target scope (R2.4, b7a91f2, atlas-assistant, production) FAILED because 214 session records were lost. This equally authoritative current result conflicts with RB-401 and is not explicitly superseded.
evidence.excerpt: Rollback rehearsal RB-402: release R2.4; commit b7a91f2; service atlas-assistant; environment production. Restore completed but 214 session records written during the window were lost. Rehearsal FAILED.

requirement.criterion: The target build must pass all 60 mandatory document parsing cases.

decisions.explanation: REQ-10 (YNA-57) requires the target build (R2.4 / b7a91f2 / atlas-assistant / production) to pass all 60 mandatory document parsing cases. The linked evidence record YNA-9 (REC-9611) contains QA Lead Priya Nair's retest PARSE-622 (comment 10044, recorded 2026-11-08T14:00:00+05:30), which explicitly supersedes PARSE-601 and reports 60 of 60 mandatory parsing cases passing on exactly the target release, commit, service and production environment. The earlier failing run PARSE-601 (comment 10043, 59/60, rotated-table failure) is therefore superseded and not a current failure. The requirement's own comments contain only developer implementation claims and coordinator tracking (comments 10280-10284), which are not proof but do not contradict the verified QA result. The other linked record YNA-80 (REC-1306) is a security approval for a different service (warehouse-agent) in staging on a different commit (comment 10396), so it is inapplicable to this parsing criterion. No confirmed open defect on the target build was found in the scoped Jira data. The acceptance criterion is therefore satisfied by applicable, superseding QA evidence.

requirement.criterion: QA must verify keyboard navigation and focus handling for the handoff interface on the target release.

decisions.explanation: REQ-11 requires QA verification of keyboard navigation and focus handling for the handoff interface on the exact target scope (R2.4, commit b7a91f2, service atlas-assistant, environment production, prompt p7). No retrieved QA result matches that scope. The only passing QA result (YNA-102 comment 10508, Priya Nair, QA Lead, 18/18 cases) is explicitly for release R2.3 and commit 42d09ce, so it is inapplicable to the target build. The only R2.4 keyboard-navigation QA run (YNA-221 comment 11101, Priya Nair, QA Lead, RUN-528) is for commit 2b8e31c in staging with prompt p4 and was aborted with a rerun scheduled, so it is also inapplicable and provides no verified result. The implementation record YNA-259 comment 11293 (Sam Patel, Developer) is only a developer implementation/recap claim and does not constitute QA verification. The requirement's own comments (e.g., YNA-162 comment 10807) are developer assertions and Done status, which are not proof. The open defect HND-DEF-4 reported in YNA-76 comment 10378 (Priya Nair, QA Lead, target R2.4/b7a91f2/production) concerns handoff message delivery to the support queue (REQ-08), not keyboard navigation or focus handling, so it does not establish failure of this criterion, but it is noted as a target-build concern. Missing proof is not a failure, so the criterion is unresolved rather than failed.

requirement.criterion: Every mandatory streaming case must complete without duplicate or missing final messages.

decisions.explanation: REQ-12 requires every mandatory streaming case to complete without duplicate or missing final messages for release R2.4, commit b7a91f2, service atlas-assistant, environment production, prompt p7. The linked QA evidence record YNA-318 (REC-5957) contains a fully scope-matched QA result from Priya Nair (QA Lead) recorded 2026-11-08T14:00:00+05:30 (comment 11648): streaming run STREAM-731 on exactly that release/commit/service/environment/prompt completed 49 of 50 cases, and case STREAM-50 produced a duplicated final message. A duplicated final message is a direct violation of the acceptance criterion, so the criterion is not satisfied. No later QA retest explicitly superseding STREAM-731 was found (searches for STREAM-731 and STREAM-50 returned only YNA-318), and no linked defect or dependency record resolves this failure. The developer implementation claim on YNA-400 (comment 12057) and the requirement's Done status are not proof of acceptance. The regression result on YNA-35 (comment 10171) is inapplicable because it covers R2.3 / commit 1e6e983 / warehouse-agent / staging / prompt p5 and also reports only 24 of 25 cases passing.
